sections.h2: Where does Upson County sit between Atlanta, Macon and Columbus?
sections.html:
Upson County occupies the west central part of the state, about equally far from Atlanta, Macon and Columbus. The state legislature established it on December 15, 1824, on land the Creek gave up in the Treaty of Indian Springs of 1821, and many early settlers arrived through the land lottery. It was Georgia's fifty-ninth county, named for a lawyer who had died only four months before.

Thomaston serves as the seat of government, with The Rock and Yatesville as the other incorporated places. The county reports 326 square miles of land and 592 miles of roads. The Flint River runs unimpeded through the area, and Sprewell Bluff Park, which the county has managed since January 2013, offers trails, cabins, RV sites and an overlook.

Textile mills turned Thomaston into a social and cultural center in the nineteenth century, according to the county's history page, though cotton's hold on the economy had faded by 1900. Houses range from mill-era homes in town to timber and farm tracts outside it.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Upson County homes?
sections.html:
Upson County reached an estimated 28,500 residents by mid-2025, a 2.9% gain since 2020. Owners occupy 61.0% of housing units, and a typical owner-held home has a value of $168,700.

sections.h2: Which Upson County office answers which question?
sections.html:
You will find both at 305 South Hightower Street in Thomaston. Pick the one that matches your question: money owed goes one way, value goes the other.

  • Tax commissioner, Suite D-120, (706) 647-8931, mail to P.O. Box 409: billing, collection, tags and the payoff figure for a sale.
  • Tax assessors, Suite D-180, (706) 647-8176, mail to P.O. Box 508, open weekdays through the working day: values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, 116 W. Main Street: copies of your warranty deed.

The tax commissioner is an elected office that stands apart from both the assessors and the county commissioners. Statements are addressed to the homeowner and never to the lender, although the office sends mortgage companies a data file. After a change of lender, pass the bill along yourself.

sections.h2: How is an Upson County tax bill calculated?
sections.html:
The assessors set fair market value, which is the full 100% figure. Assessed value is 40% of it. From that 40% the office subtracts any exemptions, and the remainder, called the net assessed or taxable value, is multiplied by the millage rate. One mill represents one dollar of tax for every $1,000 of assessed value.

Your January 1 return window also matters: between January 1 and April 1 any owner may file a return proposing a value. If the assessors disagree, they mail a notice with their figure and the 45-day clock starts. For a copy of your warranty deed, go to the Clerk of Superior Court at 116 W. Main Street in Thomaston.

sections.h2: Where do Upson County tax dollars go?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's FAQ lists the uses in plain terms. Property tax pays for the administration of county government and the public school system, for public buildings, bridges and county roads, and for the courts, the jail and law enforcement. It also funds fire protection and public health and sanitation. The FAQ calls this an abbreviated list and refers readers to the Georgia Code for the rest.

The county reports 592 miles of roads across 326 square miles of land. If your bill rose from one year to the next, the county's 2026 notice of increase states the change in mills, so compare it with the rate on your statement.

sections.h2: When do Upson County bills arrive and when are they due?
sections.html:
Real and personal property statements go out by September 15, and the county FAQ places the due date around November 15. Mobile and manufactured home statements go out by January 30, and that tax comes due on April 1.

A 2026 notice of property tax increase carried a tentative county rate of 8.244 mills, up 0.391, and listed hearings on August 26 and September 8, 2026. Without the increase the rate would have been no more than 7.853 mills. Your own bill shows the final rate, since the school board and the city set separate ones.

  • The assessed share is 40% of fair market value.
  • Three bodies set millage: the Board of Education, the county commissioners and the City of Thomaston.
  • Only a U.S. Postal Service postmark proves timely payment; a meter stamp does not.

sections.h2: What is the penalty for paying Upson County tax late?
sections.html:
Unpaid balances accrue monthly interest at the January prime rate plus 3%. After 120 days a 5% penalty is added, and another 5% joins it at each 120-day mark until penalties total 20%.

Hardship can justify partial payments, but only if you phone before the due date to arrange them, and interest and penalties keep running on the rest. Before a FIFA lien lands on the General Execution Docket, the office mails a 30-day notice of intent. Tax still unpaid 90 days past the due date is open to a lien, and credit bureaus can read those public records. Paying everything owed, fees included, cancels the lien, and the office does not sell liens over the counter.

sections.h2: How do I dispute an Upson County assessment?
sections.html:
The deadline is 45 days after the notice date. Valid grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and the written appeal goes first to the Board of Assessors, naming the appeal method you prefer.

The assessors also post a field review notice letting identified representatives walk onto a property in business hours to check its value. Homestead applications may be submitted January 1 through March 31 and must be received by April 1. You must hold the house and live in it on January 1, and a stable owner needs no yearly renewal unless the deed or address changes. Ask at (706) 647-8176 which exemption amounts fit your parcel.

sections.h2: What does an Upson County seller need to do about the bill?
sections.html:
Obtain a payoff from the tax commissioner in writing ahead of closing, and see that the closing agent pays it out of the proceeds. A bill in the January 1 owner's name means an autumn seller should check who covers the current year on the settlement sheet.

Heirs and landlords should ask about each year of ownership, including any FIFA on file. A lien disappears only on payment in full, so a buyer's title company will expect a clear account. A cash purchase can settle old balances at closing and hand you the rest, which helps when a house carries back taxes, repairs or tenants.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Upson County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: Call (706) 647-8931 or visit 305 South Hightower Street, Suite D-120, in Thomaston.

faqs.q: When is Upson County property tax due?
faqs.a: Per the county FAQ, around November 15 in a typical year. Mobile and manufactured homes come due April 1.

faqs.q: What does late payment cost in Upson County?
faqs.a: Interest runs monthly at prime plus 3%, and a 5% penalty is added at 120 days and again every 120 days until penalties reach 20%.

faqs.q: What is the Upson County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice date. File in writing with the Board of Assessors and name your appeal method.

faqs.q: Does Upson County mail my bill to my lender?
faqs.a: No. Statements go to the homeowner. Lenders get a data file, and passing the bill along is your job when needed.
